[42824 Environmental Noise and Planning | Subject description]
Credit points: 3

This microcredential covers the fundamentals of acoustics and noise control from a practical viewpoint. It focuses on assessing, regulating, and managing noise impacts. Key topics include developing a Noise Impact Assessment, applying relevant noise policies, and evaluating predictions and proposed mitigation measures. The subject is designed to equip the learner with the ability to interpret Noise Impact Assessment Reports and judge environmental noise and vibration impacts from projects using conceptual acoustical fundamentals.

[42824 Environmental Noise and Planning | Learning and teaching activities]
Subject presentation includes a ‘start-up’ synchronous one-hour online lecture facilitated by an expert academic(s) overviewing the self-study online (LMS) learning activities. Case studies of environmental noise and vibration problems and solutions illustrate the policy and planning context of noise impact assessment and mitigation. The on-campus block study sessions (two full days) focus on hands-on experience in noise impact assessment- using noise and vibration recording equipment and scenario based problem-solving practical/laboratory.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[42824 Environmental Noise and Planning | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Explore policy context and measurements in environmental noise and planning problems. (B.1)
SLO2: Develop and interpret noise impact and management in local environments. (C.1)
